A network engineer analyzes a Wireshark packet capture while troubleshooting an aborted TCP connection between host 192.168.1.50 and server 10.0.0.10. The capture displays the following segment sent by the server to the client immediately following a SYN packet:

Transmission Control Protocol, Src Port: 443, Dst Port: 52140, Seq: 1, Ack: 1, Flags: 0x014 (RST, ACK)

What does the presence of the RST (Reset) control flag indicate regarding the connection state?
questions.statementEs:
Un ingeniero de red analiza una captura de paquetes en Wireshark mientras soluciona problemas en una conexión TCP cancelada entre el host 192.168.1.50 y el servidor 10.0.0.10. La captura muestra el siguiente segmento enviado por el servidor al cliente inmediatamente después de un paquete SYN:

Transmission Control Protocol, Src Port: 443, Dst Port: 52140, Seq: 1, Ack: 1, Flags: 0x014 (RST, ACK)

¿Qué indica la presencia del flag de control RST (Reset) con respecto al estado de la conexión?
questions.explanationEn: A valid accepted RST response to this SYN rejects/aborts establishment rather than completing the handshake or gracefully closing with FIN. A closed destination port is one possible cause; filtering policy or a middlebox can also generate resets, so this capture alone does not prove the cause. Graceful TCP closure need not always use four separate segments because FIN and ACK can be combined. PSH is not a guarantee of immediate application processing.
questions.explanationEs: Una respuesta RST válida y aceptada a este SYN rechaza o aborta el establecimiento en vez de completar el handshake o cerrar ordenadamente con FIN. Un puerto cerrado es una causa posible; una política o equipo intermedio también puede generar resets, por lo que la captura no prueba la causa. El cierre ordenado no exige siempre cuatro segmentos separados porque FIN y ACK pueden combinarse. PSH no garantiza procesamiento inmediato de la aplicación.

An access switch port GigabitEthernet0/12 is configured with `spanning-tree portfast` and `spanning-tree bpduguard enable`. A user brings an unapproved desktop switch into the office and patches it into wall port Gi0/12. A few seconds later, the switch console logs:

%SPANTREE-2-BLOCK_BPDUGUARD: Received BPDU on port Gi0/12 with BPDU Guard enabled. Disabling port.
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Gi0/12, putting Gi0/12 in err-disable state.

What is the purpose of this combined feature set, and what is the current operational impact on interface Gi0/12?
questions.statementEs:
El puerto de switch de acceso GigabitEthernet0/12 está configurado con `spanning-tree portfast` y `spanning-tree bpduguard enable`. Un usuario introduce un switch de escritorio no autorizado en la oficina y lo conecta al puerto Gi0/12. Pocos segundos después, la consola del switch registra:

%SPANTREE-2-BLOCK_BPDUGUARD: Received BPDU on port Gi0/12 with BPDU Guard enabled. Disabling port.
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Gi0/12, putting Gi0/12 in err-disable state.

¿Cuál es el propósito de esta combinación de funciones y cuál es el impacto operativo actual en la interfaz Gi0/12?
questions.explanationEn: PortFast skips ordinary listening/learning delay for an edge port; it does not authenticate a PC or eliminate every loop risk. BPDU Guard protects the edge assumption by disabling the port on an unexpected BPDU. The supplied logs explicitly confirm Gi0/12 is err-disabled and not forwarding. A BPDU does not by itself prove malicious intent. Remove the cause before manual shutdown/no shutdown or configured automatic recovery; do not infer an invariant LED colour.

Under which specific architectural condition does this attack succeed, and what is the standard Cisco mitigation?

questions.explanationEn: In the classic double-tagging scenario the first switch removes the outer native-VLAN tag, leaving the inner target-VLAN tag on the frame. The next switch can classify that remaining tag into VLAN 30. The mechanism provides injection and does not itself establish bidirectional VLAN access; an unrelated return path is a separate question. Keeping native VLANs unused by endpoints or tagging native traffic mitigates the classic condition, not every possible VLAN vulnerability.

Assume there is no alternate route that can resolve the static next hop if the listed OSPF resolver is removed. Router R1 contains the following static route and routing table entries:

Configuration:
ip route 172.20.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.10.2

Routing Table:
Router-1# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set

      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
O        10.10.10.0/24 [110/20] via 192.168.1.2, 01:25:30, GigabitEthernet0/0/1
C        192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0/1
S        172.20.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.10.10.2

How does Router R1 resolve the outgoing exit interface for packets destined to 172.20.1.50, and what happens to the static route if the OSPF route to 10.10.10.0/24 is lost?
questions.statementEs:
Supón que no existe otra ruta que resuelva el siguiente salto estático si se retira el resolvedor OSPF mostrado. El Router R1 contiene la siguiente ruta estática y entradas en la tabla de enrutamiento:

Configuración:
ip route 172.20.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.10.2

Tabla de enrutamiento:
Router-1# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set

      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
O        10.10.10.0/24 [110/20] via 192.168.1.2, 01:25:30, GigabitEthernet0/0/1
C        192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0/1
S        172.20.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.10.10.2

¿Cómo resuelve el Router R1 la interfaz de salida para paquetes destinados a 172.20.1.50 y qué le sucede a la ruta estática si se pierde la ruta OSPF hacia 10.10.10.0/24?
questions.explanationEn: The route to 172.20.1.0/24 resolves via 10.10.10.2, then via the OSPF route to 192.168.1.2 on connected GigabitEthernet0/0/1. The outgoing Ethernet neighbor is 192.168.1.2, not the ultimate destination. If the OSPF resolver is withdrawn and no alternative resolver exists, the static becomes unusable; this is not a universal instantaneous hardware update. CEF may pre-resolve the recursion rather than making the CPU repeat all lookups for every packet.

Assume the HSRP LAN remains operational, hellos can be exchanged and R2 has a usable WAN path. Routers R1 and R2 provide first-hop redundancy for LAN clients on VLAN 50 (virtual IP 192.168.50.1) using Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRPv2 group 1):
- R1 Configuration: `standby 1 priority 110`, `standby 1 preempt`, and `standby 1 track GigabitEthernet0/0/0 25` (where Gi0/0/0 is R1's primary WAN uplink).
- R2 Configuration: `standby 1 priority 100` and `standby 1 preempt`.

Under normal operation, R1 is the Active HSRP router. If R1's WAN uplink GigabitEthernet0/0/0 goes into a down/down state, what will be R1's new effective priority, and what operational failover occurs?
questions.statementEs:
Supón que la LAN HSRP sigue operativa, se intercambian hellos y R2 tiene salida WAN utilizable. Los routers R1 y R2 proporcionan redundancia de primer salto para clientes LAN en la VLAN 50 (IP virtual 192.168.50.1) utilizando Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRPv2 grupo 1):
- Configuración de R1: `standby 1 priority 110`, `standby 1 preempt` y `standby 1 track GigabitEthernet0/0/0 25` (donde Gi0/0/0 es el enlace WAN principal de R1).
- Configuración de R2: `standby 1 priority 100` y `standby 1 preempt`.

Bajo operación normal, R1 es el router HSRP Activo. Si el enlace WAN GigabitEthernet0/0/0 de R1 pasa a un estado down/down, ¿cuál será la nueva prioridad efectiva de R1 y qué conmutación por error (failover) operativo ocurre?
questions.explanationEn: R1 priority becomes 110-25=85. With the stated LAN HSRP communication intact and R2 operational at priority 100 with preemption enabled, R2 can take over as Active through HSRP protocol processing. This is not a guarantee of zero delay or uninterrupted application sessions. R2 also needs a usable upstream path for external connectivity.

Con comunicación HSRP LAN conservada y R2 operativo con prioridad 100 y preemption habilitado, R2 puede asumir Active mediante el procesamiento HSRP. No garantiza retardo cero ni sesiones de aplicación sin interrupción. R2 también necesita salida utilizable para conectividad externa.

options.optionTextEn: R1's priority decreases to 95; R1 remains the Active router because HSRP requires an Active router failure rather than a priority decrement to trigger failover.
options.optionTextEs: La prioridad de R1 disminuye a 95; R1 permanece como router Activo porque HSRP requiere un fallo del router Activo en lugar de una reducción de prioridad para activar la conmutación.
options.explanationEn: 110 - 25 equals 85, not 95; and preemption specifically allows an eligible standby router with higher priority to take over.
options.explanationEs: 110 - 25 es igual a 85, no 95; y el preemption permite específicamente que un router en standby con mayor prioridad asuma el rol activo.

options.optionTextEs: R1 restablece inmediatamente su prioridad a 0 y apaga su interfaz LAN Gi0/0/1 para forzar la renovación del lease DHCP del cliente.
options.explanationEn: Interface tracking modifies HSRP priority by the configured decrement value; it does not set priority to 0 or shut down LAN interfaces.
options.explanationEs: El interface tracking modifica la prioridad HSRP por el valor de decremento configurado; no establece la prioridad en 0 ni apaga las interfaces LAN.

options.optionTextEn: R1 remains Active at priority 110 because preemption is not supported when tracking decrement is greater than 10.
options.optionTextEs: R1 permanece Activo con prioridad 110 porque el preemption no es compatible cuando el decremento de tracking es superior a 10.
options.explanationEn: The configured decrement is 25, so R1 becomes 85; a decrement larger than 10 does not disable preemption.
options.explanationEs: El decremento configurado es 25, por lo que R1 queda en 85; superar 10 no deshabilita preemption.

questions.reviewCorrection: Se elimina failover instantáneo y se explicitan comunicación HSRP y camino de respaldo operativo.

questions.statementEn: A network engineer configures a Cisco IOS router as a local DHCP server for branch LAN subnet 192.168.10.0/24. Key infrastructure devices—including network printers, switches, and servers—are assigned static IP addresses from 192.168.10.1 through 192.168.10.25. Shortly after branch workstations are powered on, users report duplicate IP address conflict warnings, and network printers become unreachable. What was the root configuration omission that allowed the DHCP server to lease statically assigned IP addresses to dynamic clients?
questions.statementEs: Un ingeniero de red configura un router Cisco IOS como servidor DHCP local para la subred LAN de una sucursal 192.168.10.0/24. Los dispositivos de infraestructura clave (incluidas impresoras de red, switches y servidores) tienen asignadas direcciones IP estáticas desde 192.168.10.1 hasta 192.168.10.25. Poco después de encender las estaciones de trabajo, los usuarios informan advertencias de conflicto de direcciones IP duplicadas y las impresoras quedan inalcanzables. ¿Cuál fue la omisión de configuración raíz que permitió al servidor DHCP arrendar direcciones IP asignadas estáticamente a clientes dinámicos?
questions.explanationEn: Explicitly exclude the statically assigned range with ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.25 so it cannot be dynamically leased. IOS can automatically exclude its own interface address and perform conflict checks; these are not a substitute for reserving other static hosts, especially if they are offline or do not respond. questions.statementEn: Network engineers are evaluating modern model-driven network programmability protocols that utilize YANG data models to configure and manage enterprise infrastructure. questions.explanationEn: NETCONF uses XML RPC and data over a secure transport; NETCONF over SSH uses TCP 830 by default. RESTCONF RFC 8040 requires HTTP over TLS, normally TCP 443, and supports YANG XML/JSON encodings. Plain HTTP on port 80 is not an equivalent compliant secure transport. These protocols can coexist with CLI and SNMP; YANG is not a proprietary MIB replacement requirement for every deployment.
questions.explanationEs: NETCONF usa RPC y datos XML sobre transporte seguro; NETCONF sobre SSH usa TCP 830 por defecto.
